articles.title: Connor McDavid Talks NHL 27 99 Club, Macklin Celebrini, Oilers' 2026-27 Season, More in BR Interview
articles.summary: After many years of being widely viewed as the best hockey player in the world, Edmonton Oilers superstar center Connor McDavid is standing on his own in the upcoming EA Sports NHL 27 video game.
articles.body:
After many years of being widely viewed as the best hockey player in the world, Edmonton Oilers superstar center Connor McDavid is standing on his own in the upcoming EA Sports NHL 27 video game.

On Monday, EA named McDavid the inaugural member of the 99 Club in NHL 27, and the three-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner as NHL MVP spoke with Bleacher Report this week to discuss that and other topics.

A longtime fan of the EA Sports NHL video game franchise, McDavid noted how meaningful it is to be recognized as the flagship member of the 99 Club.

"I feel a little bit guilty in a sense because I made a joke about it a couple of years ago, so I feel like I maybe set this up for myself," McDavid said. "But it's a cool honor. It's a game that I played since I was a little kid. I know how big it is, what this game means to kids kind of growing up and loving the game. Every way possible, playing road hockey, pond hockey, playing real hockey and going home and playing video games with your siblings or your buddies, I know how much it means. I certainly know what it meant to me."

The 99 Club is something that originated in EA Sports' hugely popular Madden NFL video game franchise, and it has developed into one of the biggest honors in sports gaming.

McDavid expressed his belief that it can only be a good thing for hockey to have NHL 27 following in Madden's footsteps with the 99 Club, saying, "I think hockey is growing and it seems to be at a great rate. Any time we can be in the same breath as football, no matter the circumstances, it's a positive thing. I know what it means in the NFL, in Madden, to be part of the 99 Club. I hope that there will be many guys to join the NHL 99 Club. ... I hope it's something that grows over time and we can make it as big as Madden's 99 Club."

Madden may be the biggest sports video game franchise of all time, but the NHL video game franchise is sacred in its own right among hockey fans.

Fans of all ages have played and enjoyed the series since its inception, and McDavid himself is part of that group.

The six-time Art Ross Trophy winner as the NHL's leading point scorer fondly remembers some of the EA NHL battles he had with his brother while growing up, saying, "My household was pretty funny. I was a Leafs fan and my brother was a Senators fan, and we'd always play Leafs vs. Sens rivalry games. For me, though, I think my favorite memory is we always got it for Christmas. It almost became tradition for us to open the game and play later Christmas Day and get it rolling right then and there."

McDavid is 29 years old now and preparing to enter his 12th NHL season, but that hasn't stopped him from continuing to have fun with the EA Sports NHL video game series.

Peeling back the proverbial curtain a bit to offer a glimpse into what life is like for NHL players, McDavid divulged that playing the NHL video game is something they like to do together as a bonding activity.

"On the road, guys are bringing gaming systems with them wherever they're going," McDavid said. "I know in the playoffs we always set up kind of like a player lounge, and we've always got a PlayStation or Xbox going, and guys are playing each other head to head there. It's definitely something that bonds the guys even still. It doesn't matter how old you are, video games can still be fun, and certainly NHL is a great way to bond with each other."

While NHL teammates have the benefit of sitting down in the same room and playing the game together, that isn't the case for everyone.

In NHL 27, EA Sports is upping the ante with the addition of connected franchise for the first time ever. With connected franchise, up to 32 gamers can compete together in the same franchise mode.

McDavid views connected franchise as a great way to remain in contact with his longtime friends, saying, "For me, being away from home, finding a way to bond with my buddies back home and staying connected with my buddies back home has always been kind of a challenge. We've done it in many different ways, and sometimes gaming is a way for us to do that."

Another major inclusion in NHL 27 is unique, in-game presentations for all 32 NHL teams.

In an effort to make playing at every NHL arena feel as real as possible, NHL 27 features true-to-life pregame productions, and McDavid is looking forward to seeing the Oilers' atmosphere in virtual form.

"A little shoutout to our media team, they do a great job in Edmonton of getting the place going," McDavid said. "I know for me personally, skating out onto that ice, big playoff game, 'Enter Sandman' is playing, the crowd's going crazy, nothing is quite like it. I hope we can see that in the game. And the other thing for me is our anthem. The way the people scream 'O Canada' at the top of their lungs, it's such a special environment, it's such a fun place to play playoff hockey, and I hope it kind of translates to the game."

While McDavid is making history in NHL 27 with the 99 Club, San Jose Sharks sensation Macklin Celebrini received the honor of being the cover athlete for the game.

McDavid was on the cover of NHL 18, and he recalled what that was like to be part of that exclusive club.

"It's a tremendous honor," McDavid said. "I remember seeing my face on the cover of the game for the first time, and it really hits you. As fans we're always looking ahead to what's the next game and who's on the cover and what's the new features and all that. It's a proud moment to be on the cover, and something that I'm sure he's very proud of."

McDavid also had nothing but good things to say about Celebrini, who he has faced multiple times at the NHL level, while also joining forces with him as part of Team Canada at the 2026 Winter Olympics.

"He's special, there's no way around that," McDavid said of Celebrini. "Being his teammate, getting a chance to see him up close and personal, just how he works at such a young age and such a high-stress environment—obviously like the Olympics is—the kid just took it in stride. He's just himself, and I think that's an impressive thing. Obviously, playing against him, he's a tough matchup. There's no question he's one of the best players in the world, and you wanna shut him down when you can, and obviously produce as well on the other side. He's solid both ways."

McDavid and Celebrini figure to be among the biggest talking points when the 2026-27 NHL regular season officially starts on Sept. 29.

Opening night will feature five games, and one of them will see McDavid and the Oilers host the rival Vancouver Canucks.

McDavid confirmed that he is feeling the excitement for opening night even though he is more than a decade into his NHL career.

"There's always excitement opening night," McDavid said. "The first game of the season is always so highly anticipated and there's so much excitement. And then obviously opening night, to be a part of that is something we haven't had a chance to do in the last number of years, there's something to be said to play on that night. It means a lot, everybody's watching. I know I've been at home watching opening night and seeing the first look at the new season. It's an exciting night and something that we're excited to be a part of, and hoping to get off to a good start."

McDavid led the Oilers to back-to-back Stanley Cup Final appearances in 2024 and 2025 before the team suffered a first-round playoff exit last season.

Although McDavid acknowledged that a tough road is ahead for the Oilers and every other team because of how competitive the league is currently, he expressed confidence that the team will perform up to its lofty expectations.

"The parity has never been tighter," McDavid said. "Everybody can play, right from the best teams in the league right down to the teams that are vying for the first overall pick. It's tough every single night. The game is in an amazing place, but with that being said, it causes you to need to be ready to go each and every night because if you're not, I don't like your chances. We got our work cut out for us, we know that. We gotta build our program back to the standard that we think it needs to be at, and we'll do that. It'll start right away here."

With McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard leading the way, the Oilers have established themselves as perennial Stanley Cup contenders, and the expectations will likely be nothing less than that in 2026-27.

As such, the Oilers figure to be one of the most popular teams for gamers to utilize when NHL 27 is officially released for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Sept. 11.

articles.title: WWE Legend Dave Bautista Reportedly Lands Major 'God of War' Role After Ryan Hurst Injury
articles.summary: Dave Bautista is stepping into a major new role soon.
articles.body:
Dave Bautista is stepping into a major new role soon.

Per Variety's Joe Otterson , the actor and retired WWE legend will play Kratos in Amazon Prime's "God of War," a new TV series based on the video game franchise.

It was announced in January that Ryan Hurst would play Kratos in the show, but he suffered a torn bicep on set that required surgery. Had he stayed in the role, production would have been delayed into 2027.

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

The show began filming in February but had to pause after Hurst's injury. With Bautista now locked into the role, it can begin filming again. The shots that had Hurst in them will have to be reshot with Bautista.

Bautista makes sense for the role given his massive stature as a former WWE star, though it's worth noting he dropped 75 pounds for his role in Knock at the Cabin . Still, his casting should have fans of "God of War" excited.

articles.body:
Latest schedule and results from the KenoGO Australian Darts Masters, the final World Series of Darts event of the season, held at the WIN Entertainment Centre in Wollongong.

James Wade fired eight 180s to reach the final of the Australian Darts Masters then went on to defeat home favourite Brody Klinge 8-5 to end the Aussie's fairytale run.

Wade beat Gerwyn Price to progress to the final, while Klinge shocked Ross Smith, Gian Van Veen and Jonny Clayton – who was hoping to make it back-to-back titles after claiming the New Zealand Darts Masters – before coming up short in the showpiece.

articles.title: NHL's Bill Daly Reveals Timeline for Texas Expansion Team to Debut amid Ongoing Talks
articles.summary: NHL deputy commissioner Bill Daly divulged that the league could be ready to announce the location of its next expansion franchise by the end of 2026, which would allow the team to officially join the NHL by 2029.
articles.body:
NHL deputy commissioner Bill Daly divulged that the league could be ready to announce the location of its next expansion franchise by the end of 2026, which would allow the team to officially join the NHL by 2029.

Speaking during the NHL's European Media Tour, Daly told reporters , "We're moving forward in Texas. I expect ultimately we'll be in a position to bring something to the board to get their view on it. So, that's proceeding at a pace. We'll probably get together with the group again in September and kind of see where they are in the process and what they want us to do to help, to the extent they need anything. If we finalize that and the board approves it, then [at the] end of this calendar year we'll have an announcement that we're expanding to either Houston or Austin."

Per Chris Johnston of The Athletic, Houston-based billionaire Dan Friedkin has already committed to purchasing an NHL expansion team for $2 billion with an eye toward putting the team in Houston or Austin.

Daly noted that Friedkin and his ownership group are "projecting the ability to start play in 2029-30" in either Houston or Austin.

That would mark the NHL's 33rd franchise, and if it comes to fruition, then the plan is for another expansion team to be added as well in order to get to 34 teams.

The location of that potential franchise is less certain, but Daly told reporters, "We have ongoing discussions both with people in the Phoenix marketplace, but also Atlanta, and then we'll see what comes of those discussions."

Texas has been home to an NHL franchise since 1993 when the Minnesota North Stars moved to Dallas and became the Stars.

Houston is among the most populous cities in the United States, and it boasts franchises in the NFL, NBA and MLB.

Although Houston has never had an NHL team, it did have a popular World Hockey Association team called the Houston Aeros from 1972 to 1978.

Austin had an estimated population of just over one million people as of July 2025, according to the United States Census Bureau. That makes it the most populated U.S. city without a team in only of the four major professional sports leagues.

Beginning play in 2021, Austin does have an MLS club called Austin FC, though, and the team is averaging over 20,000 fans per match this season, according to Transfermarkt.

articles.title: TNA Lockdown 2026 Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights
articles.summary: TNA's annual Lockdown event has finally arrived, and the company has booked 10  matches inside cages for the show in Chicago.
articles.body:
TNA's annual Lockdown event has finally arrived, and the company has booked 10 matches inside cages for the show in Chicago.

The Hardys vs. The Nemeths (Men's Tag Team Championships)

Allie and TBD vs. The Elegance Brand (Knockout's Tag Team Championships)

Cedric Alexander vs. Leon Slater (X-Division Championship)

The System vs. Fabian Aichner, Ricky Sosa, KC Navarro and Jada Stone

Jason Hotch vs. Mustafa Ali (International Championship)

Xia Brookside vs. Elayna Black (Knockout's World Championship)

Let's take a look at what happened at this year's Lockdown PPV.

The first match on the pre-show saw Vincent and Dutch battle BDE and Rich Swann. BDE and Swann did a choreographed dance during their entrance that did not impress The Righteous one bit.

The size disparity gave Vincent and Dutch a big advantage, and they made sure to use it as much as possible. It didn't take long for this to turn into a pretty physical match, but the crowd wasn't giving them much energy.

The pace eventually slowed, which made the lack of crowd noise much more evident, but all four guys tried their best to get people to pay attention. Things picked up after Swann got the hot tag, but The Righteous were able to score the win in the end.

Result: The Righteous defeated BDE and Swann

The second and final pre-show match saw Special Agent 0 take on Trey Miguel. This was a classic powerhouse vs. high-flyer combo, but Miguel's experience kept him from feeling like an underdog.

Even with a few minor hiccups, their initial exchange helped set the pace for the match. Much like the first match, the usually loud Chicago wrestling audience wasn't giving them much energy. Some fans tried, and there were moments when you could hear more reacting, but it was still unusually quiet most of the time.

Agent 0 put up a good fight, but Miguel ended up scoring the win with a pinning combination similar to a victory roll. They didn't get much time, but they made it count.

There was a couple of audio issues during the pre-show. Matthew Rehwoldt had a funny reaction when his mic had a problem.

The Righteous have such a unique aura and presentation. It's a shame that they haven't found more fame by now, but it's nice to see TNA using them.

The TNA ring being just a bit smaller than the usual WWE ring really stands out once you notice it.

Before coming to TNA, Agent 0 was known as Big Bill Collier, and it's worth taking the time to check out some of his work on the indies.

The cage came down as the pre-show was wrapping up. After the opening video, A.J. Francis made his way to the ring to take on Elijah.

The crowd was chanting for Elijah, but it didn't help him avoid a jumping knee from Francis to kick off the action. The singer recovered and hit a big clothesline before going to the top rope for Walk With Elijah across the top rope.

Francis had a hard time getting in any offense until he was able to send Elijah into the cage wall. From that point forward, it was a back-and-forth fight that saw both men hit some big moves.

Elijah was about to win with a huge Drifter Destroyer, but Expressions interfered and saved Francis. The Drifter spent a little too much time trying to get revenge, allowing Francis to hit his finisher for the win.

These two have been bitter rivals, and they did a good job making this feel like a personal grudge. The pace was a little on the slow side at times, but neither of these guys is known for being fast-paced, so it allowed them to sell everything a bit more than usual.

The fans were noticeably more vocal than during the pre-show, and it definitely helped with the vibe during the match. This was a good choice to start the show because it won't be the match of the night, but it was good enough to wake the crowd up.

During the pre-show, Indi Hartwell had a confrontation with Daria Rae. She said every decision Daria has made has been terrible, and then she made a terrible joke about her name sounding like the word diarrhea.

Chris Bey provided the theme for the show.

The powerbomb Elijah hit while Francis was on the top rope was cool.

Allie and a Mystery Partner vs. The Elegance Brand (Knockouts Tag Team Championships)

With Rosemary out of action, Allie was forced to find a new partner to defend the Knockouts tag titles against Heather and M. The mystery partner ended up being the returning Kiera Hogan, who is a former tag team champion in TNA.

Even though this was a cage match, it was stated that the match would be contested under standard tag team rules, so only one partner was supposed to be in the ring at a time.

Allie took control right away, but she brought in Hogan after a brief exchange to allow the returning star to shine for a bit. Mr. Elegance distracted the champions by climbing on the outside of the cage so his allies could take control.

The energy in this match was high, and you could tell all four women were putting in a good effort, but the way the match was structured prevented it from being as exciting as it could have been. Having normal tag rules in a match that usually has no rules just hampers what they can do.

Heather was small enough to crawl through the cage and retrieve some handcuffs that she used to keep Allie locked to the cage wall, but Kiera was still able to get the pin to help Allie retain the titles.

This match had some bright spots, but it never quite hit its stride. It will be interesting to see is Hogan takes over permanently as a tag champ or if Rosemary will be back soon.

Result: Allie and Hogan defeated The Elegance Brand

The Concierge made some jokes about The Bears leaving Chicago.

It's nice to see Kiera back on TV. It never felt like she got a fair shot in AEW.

It felt like this match would have been exactly the same without the cage. It served almost no purpose here.

The next bout was an Escape the Cage match between Moose and TNA original Frankie Kazarian. Moose had a special entrance with a throne and musicians. As Kaz made his way out, he took a seat in the throne to mock him.

Kazarian tried to escape the cage right away, but Moose kept bringing him back in because he wanted to fight. The big man had a chance to escape through the door, but he chose to lock it instead.

This was a one-sided fight for a long time, but when Moose was about to escape, Kaz gave him two middle fingers and made him angry enough to come back in and make a mistake.

It's hard to pinpoint exactly where the disconnect was, but something about this match didn't work. Both guys were trying, but it never felt like it had the intensity a feud as personal as this one should have.

It certainly had some good moments and spots, but they didn't flow together with the rest of the match. It wasn't until the last couple of minutes that it felt like they found their groove as opponents and really started to make this exciting.

The only way to win was by escaping over the top of the cage or through the door. Both men had a few close calls, but it was Kaz who got the win when Moose knocked him through the door. They telegraphed the finish from a mile away.

The violin and cello players during Moose's entrance were a nice touch.

Kazarian does a good job of making his punches look good. It's an underrated skill in this business.

Rehwoldt calling Moose the world's dumbest fiddle was a funny line.

Moose dropped some F-bombs that were very audible.

The Spanish Fly from the cage that Moose hit was the best spot of the match.

The Knockout's world title was on the line when Xia Brookside stepped inside the cage with Elayna Black, who received a nice reaction from her hometown crowd in Chicago.

Xia talked some trash to the crowd before she and Elayna locked up. They didn't seem to be in a hurry, so both women took some time to taunt each other a few times during their early exchanges.

The pace was much slower than expected, but once Black started bleeding from her head, Brookside started punishing her by using a belt buckle to dig into the wound. It definitely made things feel more brutal.

The match may not have had many exciting moments, but the blood alone made it feel more violent than anything that came before it on the show. Both women clearly wanted this to be a memorable encounter, and they succeeded in that regard.

Black put in a good effort, but Brookeside was able to get the pin and retain her championship. This was booked differently than expected, but that ended up not being a bad thing in the end. Black is definitely going to be remembered for her crimson mask.

The audio picked up all of the trash talk nicely. You could hear everything they were saying.

It looked like Black's head may have hit the cage harder than expected when Brookside dropkicked her into it. It's definitely the moment she started bleeding.

Jason Hotch put his International Championship on the line for the first time on Sunday inside the cage against Mustafa Ali.

Hotch wasted no time going after the man who had made his family's life miserable recently. Ali tried to avoid him, but he ended up with his feet caught in the cage, allowing Hotch to drill him with superkick after superkick.

Within the first two minutes, this immediately became the most exciting match on the show so far. Both guys were bringing all of the aggression you could ask for, and they were moving at a brisk pace to make things even more entertaining.

It took some time, but Ali eventually hit a DDT out of nowhere to turn the tide in his favor. Special Agent 0 took the key from the ref and opened the door for Ali, but Tasha Steelz closed it in his face.

Hotch ended up putting Ali through an announce table with a crossbody from the top of the cage, which was instantly the best spot on the show. Hotch appeared to be bleeding from the mouth after the fall, which led to the ringside doctors tending to him.

Ali took the opportunity to steal a toy from Hotch's daughter at ringside and almost set it on fire before Hotch came into the cage to stop him. Hotch did his best, but Ali won to reclaim the International Championship.

This was an incredibly entertaining match from start to finish.

Ali had a special entrance that involved him carrying a fake Tommy gun to the ring.

Hotch's sit-out powerbomb was really good. The way he and Ali bounced a little on the impact made it look great.

Ali's suicide dive through the cage door to Hotch was awesome.

Hotch hitting a couple of spots from the top of the cage made this the best thing on the entire show.

Cedric Alexander vs. Leon Slater (X Division Championship)

The X Division Championship match between Cedric Alexander and Leon Slater had the added stipulation that if Slater lost, his TNA records would be wiped from existence, meaning his record-breaking reign would no longer be recognized.

As soon as the bell rang, they started trading shots and didn't stop for a long time. Slater was the first one to take control with a couple of running kicks and a hurricanrana from the top rope.

Slater was bleeding from the head after a while, and it really stuck out against Alexander's all-white gear. Since this was also a Last Man Standing match, they never wasted time with pinfall attempts.

They didn't start milking the possible 10-count until later in the match after both men had taken a good amount of damage.

It was going to be hard to match the level of excitement in Ali vs. Hotch, but they did a good job making this bout feel different while still being enjoyable. Alexander and Slater are both very talented, so there was little doubt that this would be good.

Slater stole Alexander's finisher and hit three Lumbar Checks in a row before nailing the swanton 450. Ced was unable to answer the count, which made Slater the winner and new X Division champion.

Avery Styles appeared before this match. He had almost the exact same logo as his dad for the tron. He announced he is officially signed with TNA. Kaz welcomed him to TNA and said he can always trust him.

It will never stop being weird to see Alexander with vampire fangs.

Alexander's Michinoku Driver from the middle rope was great.

The eight-person Lethal Lockdown match was up next. A new competitor entered the ring every two minutes. Once everyone was inside, weapons became available to use. You can't win until everyone is in the ring.

Bear Bronson, Eddie Edwards, Bryan Myers and Alisha Edwards took on Fabian Aichner, Ricky Sosa, KC Navarro and Jada Stone.

The System had the advantage with entries, so they had the numbers advantage multiple times until all eight people were in the match. There were a lot of moving parts in this bout, but they didn't make it too hard to follow.

They had some good moments sprinkled throughout the fight, but it's hard to have this many people in a smaller ring than usual without it feeling overcrowded.

They made good use of the weapons, and we also got a little color during the match, especially from The System, who was able to get the win thanks to Eddie hitting a package piledriver onto some chairs.

This was a fun, violent showdown that picked up quite a bit in the second half.

Elijah was found after an attack backstage, but nobody knows who did it.

Navarro's dive through the door looked cool.

Stone's moonsault from the top of the cage was cool, but she basically landed standing up, and that could not have been fun for everyone to catch.

The Hardys vs. The Nemeths (Tag Team Championships)

Unlike the Knockouts tag title bout, this match was contested under tornado tag rules, so Matt and Jeff Hardy, Nic and Ryan Nemeth were all in the ring at the same time to fight for the men's tag belts.

Early in the match, Nic and Ryan both tried to escape the cage even though that was not a way they could win under these rules.

Nic and the Hardys are all veterans, and Ryan is by no means a rookie, so they were able to put together a decent show that played into their strengths as individuals and teams.

A table was brought into the ring, but it took them a long time to make use of it. Matt put Ryan through it with an elbow drop from the wall of the cage, but that didn't end the match.

Nic ended up htting his finisher on Matt to get the win in a moment that seemed to catch most of the crowd off guard. Several fans were shown looking baffled by the outcome.

Most of the match was fine, but the way it ended clearly left a bad taste in the mouths of many in attendance. Slater came out at the end and said his legacy in the X Division has been cemented, and he has one more goal. He challenged Nic to a world title match and handed his belt over to Carlos Silva.

The announcers pointed out that is Nic won, he would be the first person to hold the world and tag titles at the same time in 20 years.

Matt looked like he might have gotten injured early on, but he recovered quickly.

The return of TNA Lockdown was a bit of a mixed bag, but the night wasn't without its highlights.

Black and Brookside had a war that was as bloody as it was fun, Elijah and Francis put on a good show, and Slater regained the X Division title only to turn it over for a world title shot at Bound for Glory.

However, the highlight of the night was Ali vs. Hotch. Those two delivered a match that blew everything else on the show out of the water.

Avery Styles joining TNA is going to be met with mixed reactions online, but until we see what he can do, we won't know what his chances are.

The show was a tight three hours, and while some matches definitely left a lot of room for improvement, the good ones were enough to carry the PPV.
paragraphs: TNA's annual Lockdown event has finally arrived, and the company has booked 10 matches inside cages for the show in Chicago.
The Hardys vs. The Nemeths (Men's Tag Team Championships)
Allie and TBD vs. The Elegance Brand (Knockout's Tag Team Championships)
Cedric Alexander vs. Leon Slater (X-Division Championship)
The System vs. Fabian Aichner, Ricky Sosa, KC Navarro and Jada Stone
Jason Hotch vs. Mustafa Ali (International Championship)
Xia Brookside vs. Elayna Black (Knockout's World Championship)
Let's take a look at what happened at this year's Lockdown PPV.
The first match on the pre-show saw Vincent and Dutch battle BDE and Rich Swann. BDE and Swann did a choreographed dance during their entrance that did not impress The Righteous one bit.

The size disparity gave Vincent and Dutch a big advantage, and they made sure to use it as much as possible. It didn't take long for this to turn into a pretty physical match, but the crowd wasn't giving them much energy.

The pace eventually slowed, which made the lack of crowd noise much more evident, but all four guys tried their best to get people to pay attention. Things picked up after Swann got the hot tag, but The Righteous were able to score the win in the end.
Result: The Righteous defeated BDE and Swann
The second and final pre-show match saw Special Agent 0 take on Trey Miguel. This was a classic powerhouse vs. high-flyer combo, but Miguel's experience kept him from feeling like an underdog.

Even with a few minor hiccups, their initial exchange helped set the pace for the match. Much like the first match, the usually loud Chicago wrestling audience wasn't giving them much energy. Some fans tried, and there were moments when you could hear more reacting, but it was still unusually quiet most of the time.
Agent 0 put up a good fight, but Miguel ended up scoring the win with a pinning combination similar to a victory roll. They didn't get much time, but they made it count.
There was a couple of audio issues during the pre-show. Matthew Rehwoldt had a funny reaction when his mic had a problem.
The Righteous have such a unique aura and presentation. It's a shame that they haven't found more fame by now, but it's nice to see TNA using them.
The TNA ring being just a bit smaller than the usual WWE ring really stands out once you notice it.
Before coming to TNA, Agent 0 was known as Big Bill Collier, and it's worth taking the time to check out some of his work on the indies.
The cage came down as the pre-show was wrapping up. After the opening video, A.J. Francis made his way to the ring to take on Elijah.

The crowd was chanting for Elijah, but it didn't help him avoid a jumping knee from Francis to kick off the action. The singer recovered and hit a big clothesline before going to the top rope for Walk With Elijah across the top rope.
Francis had a hard time getting in any offense until he was able to send Elijah into the cage wall. From that point forward, it was a back-and-forth fight that saw both men hit some big moves.

Elijah was about to win with a huge Drifter Destroyer, but Expressions interfered and saved Francis. The Drifter spent a little too much time trying to get revenge, allowing Francis to hit his finisher for the win.

These two have been bitter rivals, and they did a good job making this feel like a personal grudge. The pace was a little on the slow side at times, but neither of these guys is known for being fast-paced, so it allowed them to sell everything a bit more than usual.

The fans were noticeably more vocal than during the pre-show, and it definitely helped with the vibe during the match. This was a good choice to start the show because it won't be the match of the night, but it was good enough to wake the crowd up.

During the pre-show, Indi Hartwell had a confrontation with Daria Rae. She said every decision Daria has made has been terrible, and then she made a terrible joke about her name sounding like the word diarrhea.
Chris Bey provided the theme for the show.
The powerbomb Elijah hit while Francis was on the top rope was cool.
Allie and a Mystery Partner vs. The Elegance Brand (Knockouts Tag Team Championships)

With Rosemary out of action, Allie was forced to find a new partner to defend the Knockouts tag titles against Heather and M. The mystery partner ended up being the returning Kiera Hogan, who is a former tag team champion in TNA.
Even though this was a cage match, it was stated that the match would be contested under standard tag team rules, so only one partner was supposed to be in the ring at a time.

Allie took control right away, but she brought in Hogan after a brief exchange to allow the returning star to shine for a bit. Mr. Elegance distracted the champions by climbing on the outside of the cage so his allies could take control.

The energy in this match was high, and you could tell all four women were putting in a good effort, but the way the match was structured prevented it from being as exciting as it could have been. Having normal tag rules in a match that usually has no rules just hampers what they can do.

Heather was small enough to crawl through the cage and retrieve some handcuffs that she used to keep Allie locked to the cage wall, but Kiera was still able to get the pin to help Allie retain the titles.
This match had some bright spots, but it never quite hit its stride. It will be interesting to see is Hogan takes over permanently as a tag champ or if Rosemary will be back soon.
Result: Allie and Hogan defeated The Elegance Brand
The Concierge made some jokes about The Bears leaving Chicago.
It's nice to see Kiera back on TV. It never felt like she got a fair shot in AEW.
It felt like this match would have been exactly the same without the cage. It served almost no purpose here.

Kazarian tried to escape the cage right away, but Moose kept bringing him back in because he wanted to fight. The big man had a chance to escape through the door, but he chose to lock it instead.
This was a one-sided fight for a long time, but when Moose was about to escape, Kaz gave him two middle fingers and made him angry enough to come back in and make a mistake.

It certainly had some good moments and spots, but they didn't flow together with the rest of the match. It wasn't until the last couple of minutes that it felt like they found their groove as opponents and really started to make this exciting.

The only way to win was by escaping over the top of the cage or through the door. Both men had a few close calls, but it was Kaz who got the win when Moose knocked him through the door. They telegraphed the finish from a mile away.
The violin and cello players during Moose's entrance were a nice touch.
Kazarian does a good job of making his punches look good. It's an underrated skill in this business.

articles.title: Avery Styles, Son of WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles, Signs with TNA Wrestling
articles.summary: A familiar surname is heading to TNA Wrestling.
articles.body:
A familiar surname is heading to TNA Wrestling.

Avery Styles, who is the son of WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles, announced Sunday during Lockdown that he is signing with TNA:

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

The Styles family has quite the history with TNA.

Ishaan Sharma of Fightful noted AJ Styles worked for the company from 2002 to 2014 and won multiple championships, including the TNA World Championship and the X Division Championship.

As for Avery Styles, he made his pro wrestling debut earlier this year.

This comes after WWE announced AJ Styles would be inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame as part of the 2026 class. The two-time WWE champion and Grand Slam champion was a headline name for much of his career.

He enjoyed rivalries with The Undertaker, John Cena, Roman Reigns and more and helped define an era for WWE.

Now his son is heading to TNA Wrestling in his own career.

articles.summary: International Sports News: Martina Navratilova has responded to Chicago Sky star Natasha Cloud after the WNBA player showed support for the trans community following her heated .
articles.body: Martina Navratilova has responded to Chicago Sky star Natasha Cloud after the WNBA player showed support for the trans community following her heated exchange with former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom. Cloud shared a message saying trans people belong and are loved. Navratilova agreed with parts of Cloudâs message but again raised her concerns about male bodies competing in womenâs sports.Natasha Cloud supports trans community after Enes Kanter Freedom ejectionThe comments came after a tense moment during the Chicago Skyâs game against the Indiana Fever on Sunday, August 23, at Wintrust Arena. Kanter Freedom was sitting courtside wearing a black shirt that read, âWOMAN noun. adult human female.âThe former NBA player was there as the WNBAâs debate over transgender athletes continued. After Cloud scored late in the third quarter, she walked toward Kanter Freedom and the two exchanged words. Security and Sky players moved between them before Kanter Freedom was escorted from the arena. The Associated Press reported that Cloud later met with team and league security but did not speak to reporters.Cloud then posted a message on Instagram Threads directed at trans people. She wrote, âTo every trans kid/person, You are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. Youâre loved. Youâre seen. Youâre perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me.âHer message drew a response from Navratilova, who has been vocal about her views on transgender participation in womenâs sports.âAll of those statements are fine. What is not fine is male bodies in womenâs anything spacesâ¦â Navratilova wrote on X.The exchange comes as the WNBA faces fresh attention over the issue. Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham recently said she opposed transgender girls and women competing in womenâs sports. Kanter Freedom and former NBA player Royce White have also said they intend to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft while identifying as women. Reuters reported on August 24 that both were deemed ineligible for the draft.Martina Navratilova also questions New York Liberty trans welcome messageNavratilova has also reacted to another recent WNBA message about trans fans. The New York Liberty shared welcoming messages for trans supporters, including, âHey trans fans! Glad youâre here! Go Liberty!â and âWelcome Trans Liberty fans! You are loved and you belong!âNavratilova criticized the messages on X, writing, âWow. Pretty sadâ¦I am old enough to remember when the WNBA totally shied away from anything LGB, when the cameras would make sure to show only âstraightâ peopleâ¦ how far we have come.âNavratilovaâs comments add another voice to a debate that has become much bigger than one game. The 18-time Grand Slam singles champion has repeatedly argued that womenâs sports should have separate rules around transgender participation. Her latest response came directly after Cloudâs message of support, showing that the two athletes have very different views on how inclusion should work in womenâs sports.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jonny Lomax: St Helens legend to retire at end of season
articles.summary: St Helens legend Jonny Lomax announces he is to retire at the end of the Super League season.
articles.body:
St Helens legend Jonny Lomax has announced he is to retire at the end of the Super League season.

The 35-year-old, who has not featured since fracturing his jaw in the defeat by Warrington Wolves in June, has made 388 appearances for Saints, winning five Grand Finals, one Challenge Cup and a World Club Challenge.

He won four caps for Great Britain and 11 for England, including a World Cup final appearance against Australia in 2017.

"Over the last 20 years, I have been able to live out a boyhood dream. Achieving far more than I could ever have imagined. Representing and captaining my hometown club and, of course, the pinnacle, representing England and Great Britain," he told the club website. , external

"I have been fortunate enough to meet some incredible people along the way, experiencing some incredible highs with them. As well as some testing times too."

He added: "I will retire at the age of 36, grateful for the life the game has given me, knowing I have given it everything I could, with the scars to prove it (19 operations, including 12 knee operations by the age of 26). Despite this, I still feel lucky.

"For those that have supported me throughout it allâ¦ I hope I have been able to do you proud."

Saints chairman Eamonn McManus called Lomax, who made his debut in March 2009 aged 18, "the bravest of brave in the bravest of sports".

St Helens are seventh in Super League with three games of the campaign to go.

They are two points behind reigning champions Hull KR, who they play in the final game of the regular season, as they look to secure a place in the top six and avoid missing out on the Super League play-offs for the first time.
